comment: Repo-side freshness pins for every citation in signoff/block-manifest.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `klt signoff --manifest` compares a manifest's
`content_hash` against the *cited envelope's own* claim about its input --
it never opens the underlying artifact. klt 0.6.0 says so itself, on every
pinned citation: `input: not re-hashed (content_hash compared against this
envelope's own claim only -- the artifact itself was not read)`. Two
hand-written files agreeing with each other proves nothing, so this file
records the sha256 of the artifact each citation is really about, and
signoff/check.sh re-hashes it on disk in CI. That is what makes a citation
here fail rather than rot when its artifact moves.
It also covers item 6, the one citation `klt signoff` still structurally
cannot pin: this repo's Monte Carlo envelope was produced by klt 0.2.0
(layout/requirements.txt's *original* pin), which wrote
`provenance.input: null`. A manifest `content_hash` on it would render
the item unmet/stale_evidence -- a false negative -- so the manifest
pins it not, and the freshness claim lives here instead, against the
committed netlist snapshot the envelope names.
Item 4's LVS citation no longer needs that workaround (issue #127):
it was re-pointed at a fresh klt 0.6.0 record
(`20260924-181216-50554fe`) whose `provenance.input.content_hash` is
non-null, so the manifest now pins it directly. Its two entries below
stay anyway -- `environment.layout_sha256`/`environment.reference_sha256`
are a second, independent claim the manifest pin alone does not cover
(same discipline item 3's and item 7's entries below apply).
`envelope_field` is a dotted path into the cited envelope whose value must
equal `sha256`; null means the envelope makes no hash claim about this
artifact and only the on-disk re-hash is checked.

pins.note: The composed LDO-core GDS the `klt drc` run read. Also the manifest's own item-3 pin, so all three -- file on disk, envelope claim, manifest pin -- must agree.

Re-pinned by issue #127 against the klt 0.6.0 re-run's own copy of the composed LDO-core GDS (previously klt 0.2.0's 20260825-123628-3b4e121, whose lvs envelope carried no provenance.input at all). This is no longer byte-identical to item 3's still-3b4e121-vintage GDS -- item 3 was not in #127's scope -- so this hash is checked only against this envelope's own environment.layout_sha256 and, now, the manifest's own item-4 content_hash pin (provenance.input.content_hash == environment.layout_sha256 on this record, so both agree on one value).

The schematic-derived reference netlist the layout was compared against -- item 4 requires the compare to be against item 1's netlist, so the reference side needs pinning too, not just the layout side. Re-pinned by issue #127 alongside the GDS entry above; the manifest pin covers only the layout (input) side, not this reference side.

The netlist the Monte Carlo campaign ran on. klt 0.2.0's sim envelope names it only by an absolute path from the machine that produced it and carries no hash of it, so this on-disk pin is the only freshness handle the citation has. Deliberately NOT re-pointed by issue #127: two fresher klt 0.6.0 envelopes now exist (20260925-110312-8280915, an intermediate run klt itself grades status=error, 185/12/3 pass/fail/error; 20260925-131502-808cece, its superseding, final run, status=pass, 200/200 -- see sim/README.md '#164' and measurements/characterization.md's Output row) but citing either changes item 6's klt-signoff-graded reason: the superseded run keeps reason=check_failed but is stale evidence a repo committed to append-only records should not point signoff at on purpose, while the current, correct run (808cece) flips the reason to wrong_kind (klt signoff docs/cli/signoff.md: 'the cited check did not fail on its own terms' -- item 6 still needs a klt yield report, which does not exist here). Either choice changes what item 6's unmet reason says about this block, which #127's own acceptance criteria calls a scope violation to fold in silently -- see that issue's thread for the full finding. This entry stays pointed at the original 4cb27f8 record pending that decision.
The `klt pex` run's input layout -- the same composed GDS items 3 and 4 were run on, which is what makes the (errored) post-layout leg comparable to them at all.
The extracted netlist the post-layout re-simulation was attempted against.

The aggregated per-spec-row rollup the generic envelope wraps. Regenerating it (measurements/build_characterization_report.py) without re-pinning here fails CI, which is the point: item 8 asks for a *current* artifact. Re-pinned by issue #142, by issue #154, and again by issue #118 (which re-ran the Output, Line regulation and Load regulation rows in full against the post-#116 DUT: all three rows' cited record ids change and all three flip STALE -> fresh, while all three verdicts stay FAIL -- the rollup is still 9 FAIL / 3 PASS / 4 N/A, so this envelope's own summary is unchanged). The two earlier re-pins -- both re-cut the DRC/LVS/PEX records the rollup's freshness table cites, and neither touched its 12 graded spec rows (still 9 FAIL / 3 PASS, as the envelope's summary says). #154's re-cut also flips the PEX detail line from status=pass to status=fail, which is the request declaring limits for the first time rather than a result getting worse -- see sim/pex-post-layout/README.md. Re-pinned again by issue #164, which changed sim/mc-output-accuracy's initial-condition contract (`tran ... uic`, EN as an edge) after measuring that the pre-#164 unconstrained `.op` handed 12 of 200 mismatch draws a start state that is not a circuit state (FB hundreds of volts ABOVE the VOUT node feeding it through a passive divider). The Output row's cited record becomes 20260925-131502-808cece and its verdict moves FAIL -> PASS, so this rollup is now 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and the envelope's own summary is updated to match. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see design/README.md "#164". signoff/records/t1-tier-report.json carries the same new hash on its item-8 citation, edited in place rather than regenerated: `uvx --from klayout-tools==0.6.0` on the sweep host resolves to a git build (0.6.0+g983394050cff) whose grading_ruleset_id and item texts differ from the pinned release, so `check.sh --write` there would rewrite the yardstick instead of the evidence move. `content_hash` is the only field a faithful pinned regeneration changes. Re-pinned again by issue #180, which brought sim/load-transient into conformance with the same initial-condition contract (#171) #164 established: its `tran 200n 3m` now releases from an eleven-node `.ic`-constrained operating point instead of an unconstrained loop-closed `.op`, and the bench was re-run over the full 45-corner PVT matrix. The Load transient row's cited record becomes 20260926-013955-6449a98 and its Freshness flips STALE -> fresh, but its verdict stays FAIL, so this rollup is still 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and the envelope's own summary needs no edit -- only `content_hash` moves. The row's own numbers did move: 0/45 corners PASS against the superseded record's 25/45, because that record predates #119 and measured neither the recovery-time clause (all 45 new failures) nor the 4.7uF C_out; the peak-excursion clause it did measure now passes at every corner. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "`load-transient` after #180". Re-pinned again by issue #179, which converted sim/loop-gain and sim/psrr-dc to the initial-condition contract's .nodeset-seeded .ac shape (#171) and re-ran both 45-corner matrices: the PSRR row's cited record becomes 20260926-033606-4a9ec09 and the Stability row's 20260926-040338-4a9ec09, and both rows flip STALE -> fresh (their predecessors predate #116/#139's pass-device resize). BOTH VERDICTS STAY FAIL, so this rollup is still 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary is unchanged. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#179". Re-pinned again by issue #189, which closed the two corners sim/thermal still had on the #171 solver-diagnostic gate after #178's seeding: one of the thirteen nodes in its `.nodeset` card (EA_TAIL, the error amplifier's PMOS input-pair source node) was written `'vsup'`-relative although three cold-start settles at ss/80C -- one per supply on the corner axis -- put its supply slope at 0.24 V/V, so the card sat 288 mV below the real node at vsup = 2.97 V. Correcting the classification (same measured number, absolute instead of `{vsup-0.836}`) takes the bench to 15/15 PASS with 0 of 15 corner logs carrying a diagnostic. The Thermal row's cited record becomes 20260926-095154-f6ab418 and its verdict moves FAIL -> PASS, so this rollup is now 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary is updated to match. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#189". signoff/records/t1-tier-report.json carries the same new hash on its item-8 citation, edited in place for the reason #164's note records above. Re-pinned again by issue #187, which corrected sim/dropout-vs-load's supply convention: that bench was the only one in sim/ driving EN off the VIN rail (VIN pinned at 3.63V for every corner while 'vsup' drove EN alone), which put EN 0.66V below VIN at the '*_2.97v' corners and, at fs/125C, left the VIN-sourced shutdown clamps M_ENP/M_ENP2 conducting 1.377uA/1.639uA against a 39pA/62pA leakage floor -- more than the error amplifier's whole 1.003uA tail current, so EA_OUT was pulled to VIN and the block never came up. EN now tracks VIN and the ramp's endpoint tracks 'vsup' so its rate stays the constant 266.3 V/s earlier records ran at. The Dropout row's cited record becomes 20260926-102849-0b63ae4 and stays fresh; its VERDICT STAYS FAIL (0/45, 0.32997-0.67307V against the 300mV bound, the largest per-corner change being 0.010mV), so this rollup is still 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary needs no edit -- only `content_hash` moves. What did change is that the row's evidence no longer reports a failing vout_at_max_vin_v corner: the -7.4521V reading at fs_125c_2.97v was the bench convention, not the design. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#187".
